messages.author: 15a7ca1419e0bfc2
messages.subject: Multigroup equality constraints
parts:
I am trying to do a multigroup analysis. I have constrained the loadings to be equal across groups. I want to do Lagrange multiplier (LM) tests for the individual paths in the equality constraints to see if the paths are significantly different in the two groups. Is there a way to do this? It does not look modindices gives me anything for the equality constraints.

Thank!
Robynne

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup equality constraints
parts:
On 05/07/2013 08:22 PM, Robynne wrote:
> I am trying to do a multigroup analysis. I have constrained the loadings
> to be equal across groups. I want to do Lagrange multiplier (LM) tests
> for the individual paths in the equality constraints to see if the paths
> are significantly different in the two groups. Is there a way to do
> this? It does not look modindices gives me anything for the equality
> constraints.

I'm not sure if I understand your question. If you constrain the factor
loadings to be equal across groups, the modindices will show what will
happen if you release them (one be one). For example:

example(cfa)
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
group.equal="loadings")
modindices(fit)

Yves.
